title: A Letter for the Uniform
premise: In the river city of Vellmark, on the eve of revolution, Casper Yarrow works in her father's print shop, where she has learned that survival means knowing which words to set and which to burn. When a frightened child is abandoned at their door with a sealed letter and orders to forget the sender's face, Casper discovers the letter names officers of the coming regime who murdered a reformist printer — and that her own father's silence was bought years ago. Racing to print and hide the testimony before the victors' historians can rewrite it, she must choose between the safety her family purchased with complicity and a record that may cost them everything. The book ends with the presses running as soldiers breach the door, the truth already loose in a thousand copies, and Casper, arrested but unbroken, understanding that memory outlives whoever holds power.
about_author: Noor Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed newspapers from collapsed regimes. She writes historical fiction about the people who move type, not armies.

chapters.title: The Weight of Silent Letters
chapters.summary: Casper Yarrow sets type in her father's print shop in Vellmark, ten days before the city falls. POV: Casper. She notices her father burning a private letter and lying about its contents, establishing the family economy of silence. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: During a curfew storm, a girl of seven is left at the shop's back door clutching a sealed letter and a coin purse, with whispered instructions: forget my face. POV: Casper. Her father wants the child gone by morning; Casper hides her in the type loft. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Letter Named
chapters.summary: Casper secretly reads the letter: it names three officers of the Provisional Council who ordered the murder of the reformist printer Aldous Renk, and lists witnesses still alive. POV: Casper. One name is a man her father dines with. Emotional beat: vertigo as safe silences reveal themselves as crimes.

chapters.title: My Father's Bought Years
chapters.summary: Casper confronts Tam Yarrow; he admits he printed Renk's final pamphlet under duress and took payment for silence after Renk's death. POV: Tam, in flashback interleaved with Casper. Emotional beat: shame passed down like an inheritance.

chapters.title: The Historians Arrive
chapters.summary: Victory is near; Council historian Edvard Moll visits the print shops to commission an official history and inventory all presses. He lingers over the Yarrow ledger. POV: Casper. She realizes any record not hidden now will be rewritten within weeks. Emotional beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers Faces
chapters.summary: The child, Wren, reveals fragments: she is Renk's granddaughter, smuggled out by the letter's author, a dying clerk named Ivet Sarn. POV: Wren, rendered through Casper's observation. Emotional beat: tenderness becoming obligation.

chapters.title: Finding Ivet Sarn
chapters.summary: Casper traces Sarn to a hospice across the river, dodging Council patrols. Sarn, barely lucid, confirms the letter and gives her a second document: witness depositions. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: grief and urgency braided together.

chapters.title: An Old Apprentice's Debt
chapters.summary: Casper seeks help from Jorun Beck, her father's former apprentice now printing seditious ballads in a cellar. He agrees to help set the testimony but warns that presses are being registered and seized. POV: Jorun. Emotional beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: The First Seizure
chapters.summary: Soldiers seize the Halvard press two streets away; the printer is taken in front of his children. Tam urges Casper to burn everything and send Wren away. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: terror making compromise look like love.

chapters.title: Moll's Offer
chapters.summary: Historian Moll returns privately: he knows a child was seen at the shop. He offers protection in exchange for the letter and a place in the official account — a lie dressed as mercy. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: temptation of safety.

chapters.title: Setting the Truth by Night
chapters.summary: Casper, Jorun, and Tam work nights composing the deposition pages in the loft, hiding galleys inside devotional stock. POV: Casper. Tam, setting his own confession into type, weeps at the case. Emotional beat: redemption through craft.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: A neighbor reports smoke and lamplight at odd hours; a search comes close, and Casper moves Wren to Jorun's cellar alone through checkpoint streets. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: courage discovered in motion.

chapters.title: Ivet Dies, the Record Lives
chapters.summary: Sarn dies before signing the last page; Casper forges nothing but prints his unsigned draft marked as testimony-in-progress, refusing to falsify even to strengthen the case. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: integrity chosen over expedience.

chapters.title: Tam Is Taken
chapters.summary: Council officers arrest Tam for debts to the old regime — really leverage against Casper. In custody he says nothing about the letter. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: a coward's first act of bravery.

chapters.title: Bargaining with a Corrupt Man
chapters.summary: Casper trades the coin purse and a decoy letter for Tam's release, letting Moll believe he has won. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: the bitter taste of surviving by deception.

chapters.title: The Distribution Plan
chapters.summary: Jorun maps the city: laundries, taverns, a ferryman, choir lofts — places the finished sheets can travel faster than patrols. POV: Jorun. Emotional beat: hope organized into logistics.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Jorun's assistant sells them out; soldiers raid the cellar press. Jorun destroys the plates and is beaten; Casper escapes with Wren and the master galleys through a coal chute. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: loss sharpening purpose.

chapters.title: The Last Press Standing
chapters.summary: Only the Yarrow shop's ancient hand-press remains unregistered, misreported as broken. Casper and her father repair it by candlelight while Moll closes the net. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: father and daughter reconciled over ink.

chapters.title: Night of the Thousand Copies
chapters.summary: They print through the night — the full testimony, the names, the dates, Renk's last words — as drums announce the Council's victory parade. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: sacred exhaustion.

chapters.title: Moll at the Door
chapters.summary: Moll arrives with soldiers as the last sheets dry. He offers one final bargain: surrender the record, and Wren goes free. Casper refuses; the distribution network is already moving. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: the climax of refusal.

chapters.title: Ashes and Paper
chapters.summary: The shop burns; Tam dies pulling Wren clear. Casper is arrested, but the sheets are gone — read aloud in markets, tucked in hymnals, carried upriver. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into legacy.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Years later, the old regime fallen again, Casper is released to find her testimony canonized — imperfectly, contested, alive. A young officer brings her a confiscated copy, asking if it is true. She answers: it is printed. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: quiet, durable victory.
